before:
Memphis is a freight airport with passenger flights attached, not the other way round. FedEx runs its superhub here with nearly 400 flights a day, mostly at night, reaching the continental United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and South America. The airport averages about 80 passenger flights a day by comparison.

It used to be a passenger hub, from 1985 to 2013. Republic Airlines started it, Northwest continued it after the 1986 merger, and when Northwest merged with Delta in 2008 the hub was judged redundant and closed. The airport went from three passenger concourses to one.

The name changed very recently. On 11 August 2026 it was renamed Frederick W. Smith International Airport after the founder of FedEx, so most systems and most people will still say Memphis International.

It sits seven miles south east of downtown on 3,900 acres with four runways, the longest 11,120 feet, and is shared with a Tennessee Air National Guard base flying C-17s.
after:
Memphis is a freight airport with passenger flights attached, not the other way round. FedEx runs its superhub here, and much of its flying is at night. By comparison, the airport handled 4.8 million passengers in 2025.

It used to be a passenger hub, from 1985 to 2013. Republic Airlines started it and Northwest continued it after the two merged in 1986. Delta took over Northwest in 2008 and closed the hub in 2013, and the airport went from three passenger concourses to one.

On 11 August 2026 it was renamed Frederick W. Smith International Airport, after the founder of FedEx. The airport code stays MEM.

It sits south east of downtown Memphis with four runways, the longest 11,120 feet, and is shared with a Tennessee Air National Guard base flying C-17s.

claims.why: Good sources disagree. The operator's cargo page says almost 400 a day and Wikipedia's lead agrees, but Wikipedia's own body says 250, the Commercial Appeal said about 250 in 2013, and a DePaul University study reported by Air Cargo News in February 2026 counts 164.7 peak-day flights. The operator's page also carries old sorting figures. Cut rather than pick one.
